questions.question: What is the main advantage of a thread pool over creating a new Thread for every task?
options: Threads are reused and their number is capped
Tasks always finish in submission order
It removes the need for synchronization
It makes each task run faster on one core
questions.explanation: A pool avoids the cost of creating and destroying threads and limits how many run at once; extra tasks wait in a queue.

questions.question: Which statement about execute() and submit() is true?
options: submit() returns a Future, while execute() returns void
Both return the task's result directly
questions.explanation: execute(Runnable) is fire-and-forget. submit accepts a Runnable or Callable and returns a Future.

questions.question: How does Callable differ from Runnable?
options: Callable cannot be used with a pool
Callable runs on the main thread only
Callable returns a value and may throw a checked exception
questions.explanation: call() returns V and declares throws Exception, while run() returns void and cannot throw checked exceptions.

questions.question: What does this print? ExecutorService p = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2); Future<Integer> f = p.submit(() -> 6 * 7); System.out.println(f.get()); p.shutdown();
questions.explanation: The lambda returns a value, so it is a Callable<Integer>. get() waits for it and returns 42.

questions.question: A Callable throws new IllegalStateException("jam"). What does future.get() do?
options: Throws ExecutionException whose getCause() is the IllegalStateException
questions.explanation: The executor stores the task's exception and get() wraps it in an ExecutionException.

questions.question: A program submits tasks to a fixed pool, prints the results, and never ends after main returns. What is missing?
options: A call to shutdown() on the pool
questions.explanation: Pool workers are non-daemon threads that wait for more tasks, so the JVM keeps running until the pool is shut down.

questions.question: Code runs for each task: Future f = pool.submit(t); f.get(); inside one loop. Why is it no faster than a single thread?
options: get() waits for each task before the next is submitted, so tasks never overlap
submit() runs tasks on the main thread
Futures cannot be stored in a loop
The pool size is ignored inside loops
questions.explanation: Submit all tasks first and keep the futures. Call get() in a second loop so the tasks can run in parallel.

questions.question: What happens to tasks already in the queue when you call shutdown()?
options: They are returned as a list
questions.explanation: shutdown() only refuses new tasks. shutdownNow() is the method that drains the queue and interrupts running tasks.

questions.question: After pool.shutdown(), the code calls pool.execute(task). What happens?
options: The task is queued until restart
questions.explanation: A shut-down executor rejects new work, and the default policy throws RejectedExecutionException.

questions.question: In what order are the futures returned by invokeAll(tasks)?
options: The same order as the tasks in the collection
questions.explanation: invokeAll returns futures matching the iteration order of the task collection, after all tasks are complete.
